name: UK inflation & rates
summary: UK CPI rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%; Bank Rate 4% with markets pricing about an 80% chance of a December rise
state: The ONS reported on 18 Nov that CPI rose 3.6% in the 12 months to October, up from 3.5%, with motor fuels up 33.2% on the year the largest upward driver; core inflation was 2.8% and services 3.7% (ONS). That sits inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band. After the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% in November, markets price about an 80% chance of another rise in December (Trading Economics, 19 Nov).
for_you: Rising inflation and the prospect of higher rates mean variable-rate and new fixed mortgages, and other borrowing, may cost more, while savings rates tend to follow Bank Rate. The next CPI release is due on 16 Dec.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
